port_difficulty.why: One CICS READ into a two-field record and a RETURN, no branching or arithmetic. The only hazard is exposing the COMP-3 balance as a decimal type.

blast_radius.why: Read only, so a wrong result is reversible by routing TRNR back. The program never uses the record it reads, so a bad read is loud only if the READ itself fails.

units.driving_fact: Reads ACCTDAT with the ACCTREC layout that PROGW writes, so the read must decode the same 17 byte record the writer produces.

port_difficulty.why: One CICS WRITE and a RETURN, no logic. The packed decimal balance must be written byte for byte, and the WRITE semantics (add only, duplicate key, commit at RETURN) must be kept.

blast_radius.why: Only writer of the account KSDS in the tree. A wrong layout or key is silent, the write is not reversible from the program, and every reader of the file, including any unseen nightly batch job, would see it.

units.driving_fact: Writes the KSDS that PROGR reads through the same ACCTREC copybook, and the tree does not contain the nightly batch cycle that may also use the file.
